# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Nakatani_2013_E2110_rat"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0075040>
* Models:
  * `Nakatani_2013_E2110_rat` -- `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Nakatani_2013_E2110_rat"))$description`
  * `Nakatani_2013_E2110_direct_rat` -- `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Nakatani_2013_E2110_direct_rat"))$description`

E2110 is an investigational serotonin 1A (5-HT1A) receptor antagonist from
Eisai that was developed for overactive bladder. Nakatani 2013 measured its
occupancy of central 5-HT1A receptors in Sprague-Dawley rats with
[11C]WAY-100635 PET, in the medial prefrontal cortex (MPFC, postsynaptic
receptors) and the dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN, presynaptic autoreceptors), and
related it to plasma concentration in two analyses:

1. **Dose-occupancy (direct) analysis.** Four male rats per dose were scanned
   4 h after 0.3, 1, 3 and 10 mg/kg orally, and RO was fitted against the
   plasma concentration at the scan with a hyperbolic Emax model, Emax held at
   100% (Equations 3-4, Figure 5, Table 1 "Dose-response study"). This is
   `Nakatani_2013_E2110_direct_rat`.
2. **Time-course (effect-compartment) analysis.** A two-compartment model with
   first-order absorption was fitted to the mean plasma profile after 1 mg/kg,
   and linked through an effect compartment (Equation 5) to RO measured 2, 4,
   6 and 8 h after the same dose (Figures 2 and 7, Table 1 "Time-course
   study"). The PK model was fitted separately to male and female rats
   (Figure 6), and the male PD parameters were combined with the female PK to
   simulate female DRN occupancy at 0.03, 0.1 and 0.3 mg/kg (Figure 8). This
   is `Nakatani_2013_E2110_rat`.

Both files share the same two-compartment PK model, so a dose can drive either
occupancy model.

## Where the PK parameters come from

The paper prints the PD parameters (the EC50s in Table 1 and the Results, the
equilibration half-life in the Discussion) but **no PK parameter values**:
Table 2 gives only non-compartmental summaries. Figure 6 does, however, draw
the authors' fitted two-compartment curves for each sex. The maintainers
digitised those drawn lines from the publisher's full-resolution figure and
fitted the same model to them by least squares:

* The male line is made of straight segments joining model predictions at
  0.1, 0.25, 0.4, 0.5, 0.75 and every hour from 1 to 10 h (on the log axis),
  so the fit compared like with like. Over 1,437 traced points the residual
  RMSE was 0.0016 log10 units (about 0.4%), i.e. the recovered parameters
  reproduce the drawn line to within its width. `ka` is well determined (a
  profile over `ka` doubles the RMSE outside 2.0-2.6 1/h).
* The female (dotted) line was fitted the same way over 756 points, RMSE
  0.0015 log10 units. Its CL/F and terminal phase are well determined, but
  `ka`, V1/F, Q/F and V2/F trade off along a ridge (any `ka` between about 1.2
  and 1.8 1/h fits equally well). The least-squares optimum is used; the
  concentration-time curve, which is what the model is for, is the same
  anywhere on the ridge.

Three independent checks confirm the read-back:

* The terminal half-lives of the recovered curves are 1.51 h (male) and 2.65 h
  (female), against 1.5 and 2.6 h in Table 2.
* Fitting the drawn RO curves of Figure 7A on top of the recovered male PK, with
  EC50 *and* ke0 left free, returns EC50 = 2.86 ng/mL (MPFC) and 3.61 ng/mL
  (DRN), matching the printed 2.87 and 3.6 ng/mL, with a single
  ke0 = 0.509 1/h in both regions (half-life 1.36 h; the Discussion reports
  1.4 h). A PK curve that was wrong in shape or level could not return the
  printed EC50s.
* The female PK combined with the male DRN parameters reproduces the
  simulated female curves of Figure 8 within one RO percentage point (below).

The packaged model uses the **printed** equilibration half-life of 1.4 h
(ke0 = ln 2 / 1.4 = 0.495 1/h), not the digitised 1.36 h.

# Population

Male and female Sprague-Dawley rats from Japan SLC and Charles River Japan
(Methods, "Animals"). The PK study used 4 rats per sex (1 mg/kg orally,
plasma at 0.25-8 h). PET studies used male rats (4 per dose level in the
dose-occupancy study, 4 per time point in the time-course study), each
scanned at baseline and after dosing at least a week apart, under isoflurane
anaesthesia; a pilot study scanned 3 female rats 4 h after 0.1 mg/kg. Body
weights and ages are not reported. The plasma unbound fraction was 6%,
independent of concentration. Doses are per kg and clearances and volumes are
per kg, so no body weight is needed to simulate.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Nakatani_2013_E2110_rat")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Two-compartment PK, first-order absorption | -- | Methods "Time-course study"; Figure 2 |
| `lka`, `lvc`, `lcl`, `lq`, `lvp` (male) | 2.352 1/h, 9.628 L/kg, 15.16 L/h/kg, 5.305 L/h/kg, 7.742 L/kg | Read back from the Figure 6 male fitted line (not printed) |
| `e_sexf_*` (female) | ka 1.344 1/h, V1/F 3.339 L/kg, CL/F 1.830 L/h/kg, Q/F 2.161 L/h/kg, V2/F 2.537 L/kg | Read back from the Figure 6 female fitted line (not printed) |
| Effect compartment `dCe/dt = ke0 (Cp - Ce)` | -- | Equation 5; Figure 2 |
| `lke0` | log(ln 2 / 1.4) | Discussion: CNS equilibration half-life 1.4 h |
| `RO = Emax Ce / (EC50 + Ce)` | -- | Equations 3-4 ("sigmoid Emax model (Equation 4)", i.e. Hill coefficient 1) |
| `lemax` | log(100), held constant | Results "5-HT1A RO Studies": Emax fixed at 100% |
| `lec50_mpfc` (time course) | log(2.87) ng/mL | Table 1 (5.85 nM); Results "PK/PD modeling and simulation" |
| `lec50_drn` (time course) | log(3.6) ng/mL | Table 1 (7.38 nM); Results "PK/PD modeling and simulation" |
| `lec50_mpfc` (direct model) | log(3.68) ng/mL | Table 1 (7.51 nM); Results "5-HT1A RO Studies" |
| `lec50_drn` (direct model) | log(2.64) ng/mL | Table 1 (5.40 nM); Results "5-HT1A RO Studies" |
| Residual error | 0 | Not reported (mean-data fits in SCIENTIST 2.01) |

# Simulation

The model has no between-subject variability, so each arm is one typical rat.
Observation rows sit on the `central` state with `dvid = 1`: the model has
three endpoints (`Cc`, `RO_MPFC`, `RO_DRN`) and rxode2 then returns all three
columns on every row.

```{r sim-helpers}
mod <- readModelDb("Nakatani_2013_E2110_rat")
mod_direct <- readModelDb("Nakatani_2013_E2110_direct_rat")

make_events <- function(arms, times) {
  arms <- arms |> select(id, amt, SEXF)
  bind_rows(
    arms |> mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_),
    tidyr::crossing(arms, time = times) |>
      mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  ) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
# A typical-value model has no omega; rxode2 warns about that on every
# multi-subject solve, which is expected here.
quiet_no_omega <- function(w) {
  if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w))) {
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
}
solve_arms <- function(model, arms, times) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(model, events = make_events(arms, times),
                    returnType = "data.frame", atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10),
    warning = quiet_no_omega
  ) |>
    left_join(arms |> select(-amt, -SEXF), by = "id")
}
times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 10, by = 0.025), 0.25, 0.5, 1:8)))
```

## Plasma PK (Figure 6)

```{r figure-6, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
pk_arms <- tibble::tibble(id = 1:2, amt = 1, SEXF = c(0, 1),
                          sex = c("Male", "Female"))
sim_pk <- solve_arms(mod, pk_arms, times)

# Values read off the drawn fitted lines of Figure 6 at model nodes that no
# marker hides.
fig6 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~sex,     ~time, ~Cc_fig,
  "Male",    0.75,  35.7,
  "Male",    3,      4.44,
  "Male",    5,      1.57,
  "Male",    7,      0.622,
  "Male",    9,      0.248,
  "Female",  0.75, 121,
  "Female",  3,     70.0,
  "Female",  5,     39.3,
  "Female",  7,     23.0,
  "Female",  9,     13.8
)

# Time 0 (no drug) has no place on a log axis.
ggplot(sim_pk |> mutate(Cc = na_if(Cc, 0)), aes(time, Cc, linetype = sex)) +
  geom_line(na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(data = fig6, aes(time, Cc_fig, shape = sex), size = 2) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.1, 1000)) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(Male = 16, Female = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "E2110 plasma concentration (ng/mL)",
       linetype = NULL, shape = NULL,
       caption = paste("Replicates Figure 6 of Nakatani 2013 (1 mg/kg orally).",
                       "Points: the paper's drawn fitted lines at model nodes."))

chk6 <- fig6 |>
  left_join(sim_pk |> select(sex, time, Cc), by = c("sex", "time")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (Cc / Cc_fig - 1))
knitr::kable(chk6, digits = c(0, 2, 3, 3, 1),
             caption = "Packaged model vs the Figure 6 fitted lines.")
# The parameters were recovered from these same lines, so agreement is a
# transcription check and must be tight.
stopifnot(all(abs(chk6$pct_diff) < 3))
```

## Receptor occupancy time course in male rats (Figure 7)

```{r figure-7a, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
male <- sim_pk |> filter(sex == "Male")

fig7 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~MPFC, ~DRN,
  1,     82.4,  78.8,
  1.5,   84.2,  80.9,
  3,     79.8,  76.0,
  5,     66.5,  61.2,
  7,     48.1,  42.5,
  9,     29.6,  24.9
) |>
  pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "region", values_to = "RO_fig")

ro_male <- male |>
  select(time, MPFC = RO_MPFC, DRN = RO_DRN) |>
  pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "region", values_to = "RO")

ggplot(ro_male, aes(time, RO, linetype = region)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig7, aes(time, RO_fig, shape = region), size = 2) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(MPFC = 16, DRN = 5)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "5-HT1A receptor occupancy (%)",
       linetype = NULL, shape = NULL,
       caption = paste("Replicates Figure 7A of Nakatani 2013 (male rats,",
                       "1 mg/kg orally). Points: the paper's drawn model curves."))

chk7 <- fig7 |>
  left_join(ro_male, by = c("time", "region")) |>
  mutate(diff = RO - RO_fig)
knitr::kable(chk7, digits = 1,
             caption = "Packaged model vs the Figure 7A model curves (RO, %).")
# Differences come from the 1.4 h printed equilibration half-life versus the
# 1.36 h that reproduces the drawn curves exactly.
stopifnot(all(abs(chk7$diff) < 1.5))
```

```{r figure-7b, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(ro_male |> left_join(male |> select(time, Cc), by = "time"),
       aes(Cc, RO, linetype = region)) +
  geom_path() +
  labs(x = "E2110 plasma concentration (ng/mL)",
       y = "5-HT1A receptor occupancy (%)", linetype = NULL,
       caption = paste("Replicates Figure 7B of Nakatani 2013: counter-clockwise",
                       "hysteresis from the effect-compartment delay."))
```

## Female DRN occupancy (Figure 8)

The authors combined the female PK fit with the male DRN parameters to
simulate female occupancy at the doses used in the bladder-function studies,
and checked it against a pilot PET scan (3 female rats, 0.1 mg/kg, 4 h).

```{r figure-8, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
f_arms <- tibble::tibble(id = 1:3, amt = c(0.03, 0.1, 0.3), SEXF = 1,
                         dose = factor(c("0.03 mg/kg", "0.1 mg/kg", "0.3 mg/kg")))
sim_f <- solve_arms(mod, f_arms, times) |> filter(time <= 8)

fig8 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~`0.03 mg/kg`, ~`0.1 mg/kg`, ~`0.3 mg/kg`,
  2,     36.4,          65.8,         85.1,
  3,     38.1,          67.2,         86.0,
  5,     32.7,          61.9,         83.0,
  6,     29.0,          57.6,         80.3,
  7.5,   22.8,          49.6,         74.8
) |>
  pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "dose", values_to = "RO_fig")

ggplot(sim_f, aes(time, RO_DRN, linetype = dose)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig8, aes(time, RO_fig), size = 1.5) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "DRN 5-HT1A receptor occupancy (%)",
       linetype = NULL,
       caption = paste("Replicates Figure 8 of Nakatani 2013 (female rats).",
                       "Points: the paper's simulated curves."))

chk8 <- fig8 |>
  left_join(sim_f |> mutate(dose = as.character(dose)) |>
              select(dose, time, RO_DRN), by = c("dose", "time")) |>
  mutate(diff = RO_DRN - RO_fig)
knitr::kable(chk8, digits = 1,
             caption = "Packaged model vs the Figure 8 simulated curves (RO, %).")
stopifnot(all(abs(chk8$diff) < 1.5))
```

The female pilot PET scan at 4 h after 0.1 mg/kg measured about 68% DRN
occupancy (Figure 8, mean of 3 rats); the model gives
`r round(sim_f$RO_DRN[sim_f$dose == "0.1 mg/kg" & sim_f$time == 4], 1)`%.

## Occupancy and efficacy in the bladder models

The paper set the occupancy predicted in female rats during the
micturition-monitoring windows against the minimum effective doses in two
models of pollakiuria: 0.1 mg/kg at 1-2 h after dosing (8-OH-DPAT model) and
0.3 mg/kg at 0.5-1 h (superior colliculus lesion model), concluding that at
least about 60% occupancy is needed.

```{r efficacy-window}
windows <- tibble::tribble(
  ~model,                        ~dose,        ~start, ~end,
  "8-OH-DPAT infusion",          "0.1 mg/kg",  1,      2,
  "Superior colliculus lesion",  "0.3 mg/kg",  0.5,    1
)
windows |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    min_RO = min(sim_f$RO_DRN[sim_f$dose == dose & sim_f$time >= start & sim_f$time <= end]),
    max_RO = max(sim_f$RO_DRN[sim_f$dose == dose & sim_f$time >= start & sim_f$time <= end])
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  dplyr::rename("Bladder model" = model, "Minimum effective dose" = dose,
                "Window start (h)" = start, "Window end (h)" = end,
                "Min DRN RO (%)" = min_RO, "Max DRN RO (%)" = max_RO) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

## Direct model (Figure 5)

The direct model relates occupancy to plasma concentration without delay. Its
EC50s (3.68 ng/mL MPFC, 2.64 ng/mL DRN) are close to the effect-compartment
values (2.87 and 3.6 ng/mL), which the paper takes as evidence that the
hysteresis is minor.

```{r figure-5, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
cp_grid <- tibble::tibble(Cc = 10^seq(-1, 2.5, length.out = 200))
curves <- bind_rows(
  cp_grid |> mutate(region = "MPFC", model = "Direct (dose-occupancy study)",
                    RO = 100 * Cc / (3.68 + Cc)),
  cp_grid |> mutate(region = "DRN", model = "Direct (dose-occupancy study)",
                    RO = 100 * Cc / (2.64 + Cc)),
  cp_grid |> mutate(region = "MPFC", model = "Effect compartment (time course)",
                    RO = 100 * Cc / (2.87 + Cc)),
  cp_grid |> mutate(region = "DRN", model = "Effect compartment (time course)",
                    RO = 100 * Cc / (3.6 + Cc))
)

d_arms <- tibble::tibble(id = 1:4, amt = c(0.3, 1, 3, 10), SEXF = 0,
                         dose_mgkg = c(0.3, 1, 3, 10))
sim_d <- solve_arms(mod_direct, d_arms, c(0, 4)) |> filter(time == 4)

ggplot(curves, aes(Cc, RO, linetype = model)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = sim_d |> select(Cc, MPFC = RO_MPFC, DRN = RO_DRN) |>
               pivot_longer(-Cc, names_to = "region", values_to = "RO"),
             aes(Cc, RO), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~region) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "E2110 plasma (or effect-site) concentration (ng/mL)",
       y = "5-HT1A receptor occupancy (%)", linetype = NULL,
       caption = paste("Replicates the Emax curves of Figure 5 of Nakatani 2013.",
                       "Points: the direct model 4 h after 0.3, 1, 3 and 10 mg/kg."))

# The direct model at the plasma concentration it was fitted against must be
# the closed-form Emax.
stopifnot(all(abs(sim_d$RO_MPFC - 100 * sim_d$Cc / (3.68 + sim_d$Cc)) < 1e-6))
```

Driven by the PK model, the direct model predicts 4-h plasma concentrations
of `r paste(signif(sim_d$Cc, 2), collapse = ", ")` ng/mL and MPFC occupancy of
`r paste(round(sim_d$RO_MPFC), collapse = ", ")`% after 0.3, 1, 3 and
10 mg/kg. The PET rats of Figure 5 had higher plasma concentrations at the
scan: read from the figure, roughly 1-2, 5-17, 20-60 and 70-350 ng/mL for
the four dose levels, so about twice the PK-study prediction at 0.3 and
1 mg/kg and increasingly more than dose-proportional at 3 and 10 mg/kg, where
the observed occupancy was essentially complete. The PK model was fitted to
the 1 mg/kg PK study only and assumes linear kinetics; it should not be used
to predict occupancy at doses above 1 mg/kg, and the direct model is best
driven by measured plasma concentrations.

# PKNCA validation

Table 2 of the paper reports non-compartmental parameters of the observed mean
profiles after 1 mg/kg (0-8 h). The simulation below applies PKNCA to the
model profile over the same window.

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim_pk |>
  filter(time <= 8, !is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, sex, time, Cc)
nca_dose <- pk_arms |> mutate(time = 0) |> select(id, sex, time, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | sex + id,
                             concu = "ng/mL", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | sex + id, doseu = "mg/kg")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 8, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        auclast = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj,
                                          intervals = intervals))
```

```{r nca-compare}
# Table 2 prints Cmax in 'ug/mL' and AUC in 'ug*hr/mL'; Figure 6 shows the
# same profiles in ng/mL (male Cmax about 48 ng/mL), so the table's units are
# taken as ng/mL and ng*h/mL.
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~sex,     ~cmax, ~tmax, ~auclast, ~half.life,
  "Male",    48.1,  0.5,   71.8,     1.5,
  "Female", 125.7,  1,    487.9,     2.6
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_res, published, by = "sex",
  params = c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast", "half.life"),
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "h", auclast = "ng*h/mL", half.life = "h")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated (model) vs Table 2 (observed mean profile) NCA.")
```

The reference values are NCA of the *observed* mean data, whereas the
simulation is the fitted curve, so the comparison measures the authors' fit
rather than the transcription. The half-lives agree. The male Cmax and
AUC0-8 are below the observed values because the fitted line passes under the
observed peak (Figure 6: 48.1 ng/mL observed at 0.5 h, about 41 ng/mL on the
line), and the model's Tmax falls between the 0.25 and 0.5 h sampling times.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **PK parameters read back from a figure.** The paper prints no PK
  parameters. They were recovered by digitising the authors' drawn fitted
  lines in Figure 6 and fitting the same two-compartment model to them (RMSE
  0.0016 and 0.0015 log10 units). The female `ka`, V1/F, Q/F and V2/F are not
  individually identifiable from the line (they trade off along a ridge); the
  curve they produce is. All PK parameters are apparent oral values, because
  intravenous data and bioavailability are not available.
* **Equilibration rate constant.** The packaged ke0 uses the printed
  half-life of 1.4 h. The Figure 7A curves are reproduced exactly by 1.36 h,
  which rounds to 1.4 h; the difference is at most about one RO percentage
  point. The paper reports one equilibration half-life, and the drawn curves
  show the two regions share it.
* **Hill coefficient.** Methods call the time-course model a "sigmoid Emax
  model" but refer to Equation 4, which has no Hill coefficient; a Hill
  coefficient of 1 reproduces the drawn curves of Figure 7A with the printed
  EC50s, so none is included.
* **Emax.** Held at 100% in both models; the Results state it for the direct
  model, and the free fit of the Figure 7A curves at Emax = 100% recovers the
  printed time-course EC50s.
* **Separate PK fits by sex.** The authors fitted each sex separately; the
  female set is encoded as log-scale offsets selected by `SEXF`. The PD
  parameters were estimated in male rats only and are applied unchanged to
  females, as in Figure 8.
* **Direct model driven by the PK model.** The paper fitted the direct model
  to RO against measured plasma concentrations at the scan. To make it
  simulatable from a dose, `Nakatani_2013_E2110_direct_rat` carries the same
  PK model as the time-course file. The PET rats of the dose-occupancy study
  had higher 4-h plasma concentrations than this PK model predicts (about
  twofold at 0.3-1 mg/kg and more at 3-10 mg/kg, Figure 5), so dose-driven
  predictions under-estimate their occupancy.
* **Dose range of the PK model.** The PK model comes from a single 1 mg/kg
  dose and is linear; the paper gives no evidence on dose proportionality
  beyond Figure 5, which suggests exposure rises more than proportionally
  above 1 mg/kg. The female simulations of Figure 8 (0.03-0.3 mg/kg) are
  below the fitted dose and are reproduced as the authors made them.
* **No variability.** All fits were to mean data with SCIENTIST; no
  between-animal variability or residual error was reported, so the residual
  terms are set to zero.
* **Table 2 units.** Table 2 prints Cmax in ug/mL and AUC in ug*hr/mL, which
  are inconsistent with Figure 6 by a factor of 1000; ng/mL and ng*h/mL are
  used. Its title also mentions spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRs), for
  which no column is given.
* **Unbound and brain concentrations.** The EC50s are total plasma (or
  plasma-equivalent effect-site) concentrations. The paper converts them to
  unbound values with the 6% unbound fraction (MPFC 0.22, DRN 0.16 ng/mL for
  the direct model) and discusses a further tenfold P-glycoprotein efflux at
  the blood-brain barrier; neither conversion enters the model.
